question: What is the primary definition of urinary retention?

options.A: The inability to completely empty the bladder
options.B: The involuntary leakage of urine during coughing
options.C: The frequent passing of very small urine volumes
options.D: The total absence of urine production by kidneys

explanation: Urinary retention specifically refers to the body's inability to expel urine stored in the bladder, leading to incomplete emptying. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h1)

question: How does urinary retention differ fundamentally from urinary incontinence?

options.A: Retention requires dialysis, while incontinence requires immediate surgery
options.B: Retention involves urine accumulation, while incontinence involves involuntary leakage
options.C: Retention causes painful urination, while incontinence is always painless
options.D: Retention affects only females, while incontinence affects only males

explanation: While both are common lower urinary tract disorders, retention is characterized by holding onto urine the body wants to expel, whereas incontinence is the uncontrolled loss of urine. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h1)

question: A common mechanical obstruction causing urinary retention in older men is...
explanation: Enlargement of the prostate gland physically squeezes the urethra, making it difficult for urine to pass out of the bladder. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h2)

question: Why do certain drugs like antihistamines trigger urinary retention?

options.A: They cause the kidneys to produce excessive amounts of urine
options.B: They irritate the mucosal lining of the bladder wall
options.C: They impair the contraction of the detrusor muscle
options.D: They physically block the opening of the ureters

explanation: Many medications have anticholinergic properties that prevent the bladder muscle from squeezing strongly enough to empty properly. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h2)

question: What is a defining feature of acute urinary retention?

options.A: Continuous dribbling of large urine volumes
options.B: Sudden onset with severe suprapubic pain
options.C: Gradual accumulation of urine without any pain
options.D: Completely normal bladder fullness on palpation

explanation: Acute retention hits abruptly and causes intense discomfort because the bladder distends rapidly over a short period. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h3)

question: Why do patients with chronic urinary retention often experience overflow incontinence?

options.A: Frequent antibiotic use irritates the bladder lining and causes leakage
options.B: The kidneys suddenly start producing more urine than the bladder can hold
options.C: The urethral sphincter completely relaxes due to chronic nerve damage
options.D: The overstretched bladder leaks when intravesical pressure exceeds sphincter resistance

explanation: When a chronically full bladder reaches its limit, small amounts of urine escape past the tight sphincter, mimicking simple incontinence. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h3)

question: What physical finding is most characteristic of a severely distended bladder?

options.A: A dull, rounded mass in the suprapubic region
options.B: A soft, flat abdomen with no tenderness on palpation
options.C: Sharp rebound tenderness in the right lower quadrant
options.D: Hyperactive bowel sounds heard over the lower quadrants

explanation: A full bladder pushes upward out of the pelvis and presents as a palpable, dull-sounding mass just above the pubic bone. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h4)

question: A male patient post-surgery cannot urinate for six hours and has lower belly pain. What is your immediate nursing assessment step?

options.A: Administer a strong oral diuretic medication as prescribed
options.B: Document the finding as normal post-operative urinary hesitancy
options.C: Palpate and perkuss the suprapubic area for bladder distention
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink two liters of water immediately

explanation: Checking for a palpable bladder confirms whether urine is actually accumulating before taking further clinical action. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h4)

question: What non-invasive device is commonly used at the bedside to measure bladder volume?
explanation: A bladder scanner calculates urine volume inside the bladder safely and quickly without inserting any tubes. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h5)

question: Why are serum creatinine and urea tests ordered for a patient with severe urinary retention?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of urine left inside the bladder
options.B: To calculate the correct dosage of antibiotics needed for treatment
options.C: To check if bladder backpressure has started harming the kidneys
options.D: To determine the specific bacterial infection causing the blockage

explanation: Longstanding high pressure in the urinary tract travels upward to the kidneys, impairing their filtration ability and elevating blood waste levels. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h5)

question: What is the immediate priority treatment for acute urinary retention?

options.A: Immediate surgical removal of the prostate gland
options.C: Continuous bladder irrigation with sterile water

explanation: Relieving the agonizing pressure by draining accumulated urine through a catheter is the urgent first step. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h6)

question: How do alpha-blockers help manage urinary retention caused by an enlarged prostate?

options.A: They dissolve the fibrous tissue obstructing the urethral lumen
options.B: They relax the smooth muscle fibers in the prostate and bladder neck
options.C: They stop the kidneys from making more urine during the night
options.D: They paralyze the bladder wall to stop painful muscle spasms

explanation: Alpha-blockers ease the squeeze around the urethra, allowing urine to flow more freely without immediate surgery. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h6)

question: Why should a nurse avoid draining a massive volume of urine all at once?

options.A: Total drainage stops the kidneys from producing any further urine
options.B: It forces air bubbles into the bladder and causes severe pain
options.C: Rapid decompression can cause bleeding and sudden blood pressure drops
options.D: It will immediately cause the catheter balloon to burst inside

explanation: Sudden reduction of intravesical pressure causes mucosal vessel rupture and rapid fluid shifts, risking shock and severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h7)

question: You have inserted a catheter for acute retention and 1200 mL drains rapidly. What is your best action based on safety guidelines?

options.A: Inject sterile water into the balloon to secure the tubing in place
options.B: Clamp the tubing temporarily to control the rate of bladder decompression
options.C: Remove the catheter immediately and notify the doctor of the high volume
options.D: Administer a rapid intravenous fluid bolus to prevent dehydration

explanation: Gradual drainage prevents sudden pressure changes within the bladder and protects the patient from hemorrhage and shock. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h7)

question: What is a severe systemic complication of untreated urinary retention?
explanation: Stagnant, retained urine serves as a breeding ground for bacteria, which can easily invade the bloodstream and cause life-threatening sepsis. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h8)

question: Why is keeping the urinary drainage bag below the level of the bladder crucial?

options.A: It prevents backflow of contaminated urine into the bladder
options.B: It speeds up the rate of urine production by the kidneys
options.C: It keeps the catheter balloon inflated inside the bladder
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling the urge to urinate

explanation: Gravity ensures urine flows downward away from the body; lifting the bag above the bladder pushes bacteria straight back inside. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T16#GNS212_U1_T16_h8)
